open_points.subject: answer_request
open_points.text: - answer_request: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST check one request in exactly this order, the first failure deciding: the byte length of request_bytes is within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SURFACE_REQUEST_BYTES_MAX constant, else invalid_request; authenticate_token with presented_token gives an Actor, else unauthorized with one fixed reason that reveals nothing about any record; the depth check of the request message below, else invalid_request; for tools/call, the message names a catalogue operation, fits that operation's request model with no unknown field — a field typed X | None fitting when it is absent or JSON null; the fit is pydantic's in JSON mode, the request model's model_validate_json over the canonical JSON text of the arguments with strict=True, since strict validation of Python objects refuses an enum given as its value string and a tuple given as a JSON array, which is how every request carries them; a ValueError the fit raises (pydantic's ValidationError is one) is raised again as InvalidRequestError, so translate_failure answers invalid_request, never internal_error —, holds every bound below, measured on the fitted request before any JSON text in it is replaced, and has every JSON text it carries then made canonical by the replacement below, else invalid_request; the actor may call that operation by the actor table, else raise NotPermittedError; only then is the operation's handler called (A16 rule 1). initialize, ping and tools/list name no catalogue operation and are answered after the depth check, as the note on methods says.
open_points.other_text: from cabinet_kernel.store import InvalidRequestError, RefusedError, StoreInternalError, UnknownReferenceError, open_store, page_records, read_records, read_value_bytes
open_points.question: Must NotPermittedError be added to IMPORTS, or must answer_request raise one of the imported exception types instead?

open_points.subject: translate_failure
open_points.text: - translate_failure: [FIELD_PROJECTION] MUST map a failure to its code of = models.RefusalCode: UnknownReferenceError to unknown_reference, NotPermittedError to not_permitted, RefusedError to refused, InvalidRequestError and NonCanonicalValueError to invalid_request; StoreInternalError, StopRequiredError and every other exception to internal_error.
open_points.other_text: from cabinet_kernel.store import InvalidRequestError, RefusedError, StoreInternalError, UnknownReferenceError, open_store, page_records, read_records, read_value_bytes
open_points.question: Must NotPermittedError be added to IMPORTS, or must translate_failure omit or replace this mapping?
